title: Advanced Sample Handling for Surface Chemical Analysis in Materials Development
content: As interest in energy conversion and storage continues to grow, the materials systems and combinations employed to this purpose continue to expand, requiring analytical capabilities to envelop an increasing mix of chemistries for characterization. These new materials systems require investigations of interface bonding and degradation mechanisms, which expands the application of surface characterization techniques, with X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) seeing broad interest and application across the entire range. The utility of XPS in this domain is due to its capability to provide chemical state information in the first few atomic layers of a material, due to the exponential decay of the signal intensity deeper into the sample.
